No Front Lines: A Decision Guide for Companies Caught in Conflict
news.summary_en: Companies that never considered themselves defense companies are now on the front lines. This report explores how companies can navigate the fog of conflict and mitigate risks, as well as how the U.S. government can assess and reduce the threats they face.

news.title: Did the United States and Russia Just Agree to Collaborate on Data Centers?
news.summary_en: A joint data center proposed as part of broader negotiations between the United States and Russia poses a substantive threat to U.S. national security. Congress should play a vital role in scrutinizing the idea before it becomes a reality.

news.title: Ukraine and South Korea’s Diplomatic Dispute Deepens | State of Play
news.summary_en: Victor Cha explains why the diplomatic dispute between South Korea and Ukraine over President Volodymyr Zelensky’s public disclosure that Kyiv had transferred two North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul has deepened, and what both sides may want out of it.

news.title: Will AI Concerns Become a New Source of Terrorism?
news.summary_en: What is the risk that fears about AI will motivate terrorist attacks? This analysis examines the record of anti-AI violence so far, how and why new terrorist causes emerge, and what that history suggests for AI-related violence.

news.title: Throttling Starlink Is a Disaster for Ukraine and the United States
news.summary_en: In demonstrating its unreliability as a security partner, the United States is eroding allied trust in U.S. defense and technology suppliers and in NATO.

news.title: Sustaining South Africa’s Progress in the Next Phase of the HIV Fight
news.summary_en: South Africa has 8 million people living with HIV, and the government has introduced lenacapavir, a new HIV prevention drug. Thousands have started on the injections, but questions about future costs and supplies will need to be resolved to ensure the campaign’s success.

news.title: Risk to Refugee Return
news.summary_en: This installment of Charting the Middle East highlights how the scale of unexploded ordnance (UXO) contamination, relative to returning populations, varies across Syria.
